newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan has 3.6 million child workers - survey.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan has 3.6 million child workers - survey.

text.p: About 3.6 million children aged five to 14 work full time in Pakistan, many of them spending long hours in unskilled jobs where some fall sick or get injured, a child labour survey released on Wednesday said.

"The total number of economically active children would be 3.6 million, representing about nine percent of the children between five and 14 years of age," said the survey compiled jointly by the International Labour Organisation, Pakistan's Labour Ministry and the Federal Bureau of Statistics.
The survey said about 71 percent of Pakistan's child labourers held unskilled jobs in agriculture, sales and services, mining, construction, manufacturing and transport.
"About 46 percent work more than the normal working hours of 35 hours per week. A good proportion of the children at the national level work 56 hours or more," it said.
The survey said about seven percent of the child workers frequently suffered from illness and injury, and 28 percent occasionally. Most such problems were in the farm sector.
Labour Minister Ghulam Akbar Lasi said the survey supported Pakistan's position that "malicious propaganda" by foreign media and other groups had exaggerated the child labour problem.

"Exaggerated statistics and figures were released by various agencies about the size of child labour incidence in Pakistan to the international media, which used (them) to damage Pakistan's economic interest and tarnish its image," Lasi said.
"Pakistan has been contesting these highly exaggerated figures and its position stands vindicated now, as the child labour survey...reveals," he added.

Lasi said the results of the survey would be used as a basis for actions to improve children's lot. "We need to withdraw our children from workplaces and integrate them in the stream of education in a healthy climate," he said.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) estimated last year that 10 million children -- out of Pakistan's total population of more than 130 million -- were employed in brick kilns, farms, carpet manufacturing, workshops and restaurants.
In June, Pakistan, faced with scathing international criticism and threats of trade sanctions, ordered local authorities to raid factories employing child labour.
